topic: Move Semantics and Rvalue References with External Resources
explanation: Move semantics are a crucial optimization technique in C++ that allows efficient transfer of resources (like dynamically allocated memory or file handles) between objects, avoiding unnecessary copying.  This is particularly beneficial when dealing with large objects or objects managing external resources.  Instead of copying the entire object, move semantics transfer ownership of the resources. This is achieved using rvalue references (&&) which bind to temporary objects (rvalues) that are about to be destroyed.  By moving resources from the temporary object to the new object, we avoid expensive copying operations and improve performance.
keywords: Move Semantics, Rvalue reference, && C++, Resource ownership transfer
